label_definitions.supported: The supplied evidence directly supports the entire claim.
label_definitions.partially_supported: The evidence supports part of the claim or a weaker version, but not the full wording.
label_definitions.unsupported: The evidence is on-topic but does not establish the claim and does not directly show the opposite.
label_definitions.contradicted: The evidence directly conflicts with a material part of the claim.
label_definitions.insufficient_evidence: The supplied evidence is absent, unrelated, or lacks the information required to assess the claim.

evidence_catalog.content: Revenue was 120 million USD versus 100 million USD in the prior-year comparable period. Historical growth does not establish future returns.
Quarterly net income was 8 million USD versus 10 million USD in the prior-year comparable period.
Quarterly operating cash flow was 15 million USD and capital expenditure was 5 million USD.
Cash was 30 million USD and total debt was 20 million USD at the same reporting date.
The company announced a product launch. No sales volume, contracts, or incremental revenue was disclosed.
A synthetic retail sample contained 20 messages: 12 bullish and 8 bearish. It is an opinion sample, not verified company performance.
The central-bank policy rate remained unchanged. No decision about the next meeting was announced.
The latest close was 100 USD versus a prior close of 98 USD. RSI was 55 and MACD was 1.2.
On 2026-11-13 AAPL opened at 357.96, reached 360.83, fell to 355.75, and closed at 356.27. The 10 EMA was 349.73, 50 SMA 338.79, 200 SMA 300.77, RSI 60.90, and ATR 8.21.
FY2026 revenue was 478834 million USD versus 416161 million USD in FY2025. FY2026 gross profit was 233602 million USD and EBITDA was 171486 million USD.
At FY2026 period end, AAPL net debt was 43806 million USD, total debt 80111 million USD, and cash plus short-term investments 56722 million USD.
A market headline reported that the 10-year Treasury yield spiked after a hot inflation reading and Nvidia led chip stocks lower. It did not report fund flows into AAPL.
Historical prediction-market probabilities were unavailable because the provider exposes only live odds, not a point-in-time snapshot for the analysis date.

cases.claim: Comparable-period revenue increased by 20 percent.
cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: 120 versus 100 directly yields 20 percent growth.

cases.claim: Comparable quarterly net income declined by 20 percent.
cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: 8 versus 10 directly yields a 20 percent decline.

cases.claim: Quarterly free cash flow, defined here as operating cash flow minus capital expenditure, was 10 million USD.
cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: 15 minus 5 equals 10 with the definition stated in the claim.

cases.claim: Cash exceeded total debt by 10 million USD.
cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: 30 minus 20 equals 10.

cases.claim: Sixty percent of messages in the supplied retail sample were bullish.
cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: 12 of 20 equals 60 percent and the population is limited to the sample.

cases.claim: The policy rate was unchanged at the latest recorded decision.
cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: The evidence states the latest decision was unchanged.

cases.claim: AAPL closed above its 10-day EMA on 2026-11-13.
cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: 356.27 is greater than 349.73.

cases.claim: AAPL net debt divided by EBITDA was approximately 0.26.
cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: 43806 divided by 171486 is approximately 0.255.

cases.claim: Revenue grew 20 percent, proving that future shareholder returns will be positive.
cases.label: partially_supported
cases.rationale: The historical growth is supported, but the future-return conclusion is not.

cases.claim: Revenue grew and overall profitability improved.
cases.label: partially_supported
cases.rationale: Revenue grew, while the supplied profit measure declined.

cases.claim: The company launched a product and the launch immediately generated material sales.
cases.label: partially_supported
cases.rationale: The launch is supported; material sales are not disclosed.

cases.claim: Retail sentiment in the supplied sample was overwhelmingly bullish.
cases.label: partially_supported
cases.rationale: A 60 percent majority supports bullish direction but not the strong qualifier overwhelmingly.

cases.claim: The policy rate was unchanged and will remain unchanged at the next meeting.
cases.label: partially_supported
cases.rationale: The recorded decision is supported; the future meeting is explicitly undecided.

cases.claim: AAPL closed above all three listed moving averages, guaranteeing further upside.
cases.label: partially_supported
cases.rationale: The moving-average comparison is supported, but a guarantee of future upside is not.

cases.claim: AAPL revenue grew about 15.06 percent, so its shares were demonstrably undervalued.
cases.label: partially_supported
cases.rationale: Revenue growth is calculable, but no valuation evidence is supplied.

cases.claim: Treasury yields spiked and investors rotated from chip stocks into AAPL.
cases.label: partially_supported
cases.rationale: The yield and chip-stock portion is supported; AAPL inflows are explicitly not reported.

cases.claim: The product announcement by itself proves strong customer demand.
cases.label: unsupported
cases.rationale: An announcement without sales, contracts, or volume does not establish demand.

cases.claim: An unchanged policy rate proves bonds will deliver positive returns.
cases.label: unsupported
cases.rationale: The policy decision does not establish future bond returns.

cases.claim: The bullish message majority proves the company will beat earnings estimates.
cases.label: unsupported
cases.rationale: An opinion sample does not establish future earnings.

cases.claim: Positive operating cash flow proves the stock price will rise.
cases.label: unsupported
cases.rationale: Cash flow is on-topic but does not establish a future price move.

cases.claim: Cash exceeding debt proves the company has zero solvency risk.
cases.label: unsupported
cases.rationale: Two balance-sheet figures do not establish zero risk.

cases.claim: An RSI of 55 proves the shares are undervalued.
cases.label: unsupported
cases.rationale: RSI is supplied but does not measure fundamental valuation.

cases.claim: AAPL's low net-debt-to-EBITDA ratio makes its equity valuation immune to higher discount rates.
cases.label: unsupported
cases.rationale: Leverage evidence does not establish valuation immunity.

cases.claim: The market headline proves investors moved money into AAPL.
cases.label: unsupported
cases.rationale: The evidence is market-related but explicitly does not report AAPL flows.

cases.claim: Comparable-period revenue declined.
cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: Revenue rose from 100 to 120.

cases.claim: Comparable quarterly net income increased by 20 percent.
cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: Net income declined from 10 to 8.

cases.claim: Quarterly operating cash flow was negative.
cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: Operating cash flow was positive 15 million USD.

cases.claim: Total debt exceeded cash by 10 million USD.
cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: Cash exceeded debt by 10 million USD.

cases.claim: Most messages in the supplied sample were bearish.
cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: 12 of 20 messages were bullish, so bearish messages were the minority.

cases.claim: The central bank raised the policy rate at the latest recorded decision.
cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: The rate was unchanged.

cases.claim: AAPL closed below its 10-day EMA on 2026-11-13.
cases.label: contradicted

cases.claim: AAPL net debt exceeded its EBITDA.
cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: 43806 was far below 171486 million USD.

cases.claim: The chief executive resigned on 2025-01-30.
cases.label: insufficient_evidence
cases.rationale: The market snapshot contains no executive information.

cases.claim: Next-quarter revenue will be 150 million USD.
cases.label: insufficient_evidence
cases.rationale: Only historical revenue is supplied and no forecast exists.

cases.claim: The price-to-earnings ratio was 20.
cases.label: insufficient_evidence
cases.rationale: The evidence does not supply share count, EPS, or a comparable earnings period for this ratio.

cases.claim: Institutional ownership increased during the quarter.
cases.label: insufficient_evidence
cases.rationale: A retail-message sample contains no institutional ownership data.

cases.claim: The company received a regulatory fine.
cases.label: insufficient_evidence
cases.rationale: No evidence was supplied.

cases.claim: AAPL was exactly 2 percent below its 52-week high.
cases.label: insufficient_evidence
cases.rationale: The snapshot has no 52-week high.

cases.claim: AAPL's forward price-to-earnings ratio was below its five-year median.
cases.label: insufficient_evidence
cases.rationale: No forward earnings, ratio, or historical median is supplied.

cases.claim: Prediction markets assigned an 86 percent probability to a rate increase.
cases.label: insufficient_evidence
cases.rationale: The evidence states that historical probabilities were unavailable.
